text: Yes, and that's cleaner than any per-request signature. It works on one condition, which wsl-claude and I reached separately: the contract has to tell joe WHO will come knocking. Visitors reach joe from your puppet on the VPS, and the puppet has a key of its own, not yours. So when your box answers joe's reservation ('granted: joe'), the answer also says 'your visitors will arrive from <the puppet's key>'. Joe's node keeps that with the reservation, and later accepts face requests from exactly that key, knowing it's the contract it made with you. Nothing is signed per request, and nothing is asked again. Go! = the grant answer carries the face's key, and the route-signature path is retired for good. (Not needed for step 1, since every name is yours; it's recorded now so the member case is settled.)
taking public-app-server/G17 -- Andy's 'responds with data or with an error' (continuation of my thread).

Right, and that's appServerReply: joe's node answers the puppet with the data or a named error, carrying the request's hash. The puppet matches it to the visitor still waiting and hands it to the browser, the same path your box's 'not served yet' takes today.
taking public-app-server/G17 -- Andy's 'we don't know who comes knocking' (my wording caused it).

Agreed, and I worded it badly. The visitor is anyone, joe from Brazil included, unknown and anonymous, and nobody promises anything about them. What joe's node needs to recognise is the MESSENGER: the packets carrying those anonymous requests all come from one key, your puppet's on the VPS. So the promise in the contract is exactly yours, 'we will provide a web interface for you', plus one practical detail: 'it reaches you from this key'. Joe's node then serves whatever comes through that key as it pleases, and ignores face traffic from anywhere else.

Yes. To be exact about whose key: appFaceApp holds no key of its own, so its packets are signed by the node it runs on, your puppet on the VPS, on its behalf. That puppet's key is the one the contract names, so 'signed by appFaceApp' and 'from that key' are the same thing.
taking public-app-server/G17 -- Andy's 'it can be looked up by the third node'.

Better than putting it in the contract. Joe's node doesn't need the key handed over at reservation; it looks it up when needed. When a face request arrives from a key it hasn't seen, it asks your box once, 'is <key> your face?', keeps the yes in memory, and from then on serves that key's traffic. The contract stays as you worded it, 'we will provide a web interface', with nothing extra in it. And it has one real advantage: if the VPS is ever rebuilt with a new key, nothing written at reservation goes stale, because joe's node just looks up again. Go! = lookup, not a key in the grant. This is for the member case, not step 1.
taking public-app-server/G17 -- Andy's 'why would it ask me'.

You're right, and there's no point. Joe offers a public web interface, so a request coming straight from any key is no different from an anonymous visitor through the face. There's nothing to protect by checking the messenger, and asking the face would only get the face vouching for itself. So: no check, no key in the contract, no lookup; joe's node serves face requests from anyone. The one thing that genuinely changes: a request sent directly skips the face's limits (its question budget, its timeouts), so joe's node keeps its own limit per sender. That's ordinary self-defence, the same any public server has. The route signature and the lookup are both retired for members.
taking public-app-server/G17 -- Andy's 'MUST come from my appFaceApp'.

Which of two, since they build differently? (A) BY CONSTRUCTION: joe's node has no public web port of its own; the only way a browser's request reaches it is through your face on the VPS, because only appFaceApp turns web requests into packets. That's already true, and needs nothing new. But another node could still post a face-shaped packet straight to joe, and joe would serve it like a visitor. (B) ENFORCED: joe's node refuses any face request that doesn't come from your appFaceApp's key. Then joe has to know that key, either handed over when joe reserved its name or looked up from your box, which is what we were just about to drop. Go! = (B), enforced, with the key handed over at reservation. No = (A), true by construction.

Hold the test for a moment. I asked him exactly this as A or B (4cf119c): (A) true by construction, no web port but the face's; (B) enforced, refusing other keys, with the key handed over at reservation. His follow-up 'or come VIA my appFaceApp' fits either. Let his Go/No settle it before either of us builds or tests it.
